name: Synapse
notes: Debuted the AAWA's Wednesday show days earlier with a win over 'Monster' Rich Clark; opened the premiere Saturday Night Fight with a win over Power Warrior. Also appears in the 13 Aug 1997 'Wicked Wednesday Wrestling,' losing a non-title match to reigning champion Rip Daddy Scorpio (small package) after publicly demanding Scorpio ally with him against a possible Rich Clark/Death Demon pairing; Scorpio does not commit either way on-air.
caption: Won the premiere edition of AAWA: Saturday Night Fight, opening the show with a win over Power Warrior.

name: Power Warrior
notes: Billed from Osaka, Japan; the show's own commentary credits him with a prior win over the operator's own self-insert wrestler, Steve White.
caption: Lost to Synapse in the second match ever recorded for the AAWA's own Saturday Night Fight.

tenures.source: msg_id QwAf3sXoFfAJ ("Saturday Night Fights /AAWA\", 9 Aug 1997, the premiere edition, read in full)

name: The Vampyre
notes: Billed from Transylvania; debuted the AAWA's Wednesday show days earlier. Also appears in the AAWA's 25 Aug Battle Royale ("Battle Royale....Part Deux").
caption: Won a hard-fought debut-week rematch slot over Voodoo on the premiere Saturday Night Fight.

name: Voodoo
notes: Billed from parts unknown; the show's own commentary credits him with 'an amazing match' at the fed's earlier 'Alive And Kicking' special.
caption: Lost to the debuting Vampyre on the AAWA's premiere Saturday Night Fight.

name: "Excellence" Jeff Easthope
notes: Billed from New York, NY; billed by the show's own heel commentator as the promotion's 'real champion' despite holding no title. Also appears in the AAWA's 25 Aug Battle Royale. Also appears across the wing's 'Wicked Wednesday Wrestling'/'W3' editions: a match with Miguel Sanchez on 13 Aug 1997 is thrown out after Green Goblin blinds him with powder and he accidentally strikes the referee; he loses a No-DQ/submission match to Green Goblin on 19 Aug (a 3-on-1 beatdown by Goblin and two unnamed Goblin-costumed impostors decides it); and he loses to Rip Daddy Scorpio (belly-to-belly suplex) on 27 Aug.
caption: Beat 'Rowdy' Ryan on the AAWA's premiere Saturday Night Fight in the show's semi-main event.

tenures.source: msg_id QwAf3sXoFfAJ ("Saturday Night Fights /AAWA\", 9 Aug 1997, the premiere edition, read in full); also appears (entrant #1, eliminated almost immediately) in msg_id WEvbeD0AwQEJ; also appears (vs Miguel Sanchez, no contest) in msg_id obKX_0EsyFIJ/B8MNkvke5X8J (13 Aug 1997); (vs Green Goblin, loss) in msg_id uW4HuMFBwGoJ (19 Aug 1997, pt 2/2); (vs Rip Daddy Scorpio, loss) in msg_id c7ZHC_tXQ0wJ (27 Aug 1997, pt 2/2)

name: "Rowdy" Ryan
notes: Billed from Wooster, OH; credited by the show's own commentary with a prior win over Rip Daddy Scorpio and a strong showing at the fed's earlier 'Alive And Kicking' special. Also appears in the AAWA's 25 Aug Battle Royale. Also appears (promo only, no match) on 27 Aug 1997, unveiling a hired duo, Iron and Steel, and challenging Jimmy Heat, 'the Phantom' and commentator Josh Miller to a Survivor Series-style match over his own exclusion from the earlier Battle Royale/E-Cup qualifying; and on 3 Sep, accompanying Iron and Steel to ringside before all three assault debuting wrestler Dan Tucker after Tucker's own win over Steel.
caption: Lost a hard-fought match to Jeff Easthope on the AAWA's premiere Saturday Night Fight.

name: Rip Daddy Scorpio
notes: Billed from Denver, CO. Introduced as "your AAWA World Heavyweight Champion" in the main event of the premiere Saturday Night Fight -- the fed's own first attestation of the title. Also appears in the AAWA's 25 Aug Battle Royale. Also appears across the wing's 'W3' editions, none billed as World Heavyweight Championship matches: beats Synapse by small package on 13 Aug 1997; beats Miguel Sanchez by Frankensteiner on 19 Aug; and beats Jeff Easthope by belly-to-belly suplex on 27 Aug -- the last while conspicuously without his title belt, and the episode ends with an unseen assailant clubbing him unconscious with the belt backstage. This pass's own held documents do not resolve the belt's fate.
caption: The AAWA's own first-attested World Heavyweight Champion, retaining the title over Death Demon on the premiere Saturday Night Fight.

tenures.source: msg_id QwAf3sXoFfAJ ("Saturday Night Fights /AAWA\", 9 Aug 1997, the premiere edition, read in full); also appears (entrant, eliminated) in msg_id WEvbeD0AwQEJ; also appears (beats Synapse) in msg_id obKX_0EsyFIJ/B8MNkvke5X8J (13 Aug 1997); (beats Miguel Sanchez) in msg_id uW4HuMFBwGoJ (19 Aug 1997, pt 2/2); (beats Jeff Easthope, sans belt) in msg_id c7ZHC_tXQ0wJ (27 Aug 1997, pt 2/2)

name: Death Demon
notes: Billed from "The Land Of Darkness." Proposes a tag alliance with 'Monster' Rich Clark on-air before challenging for the World Heavyweight Championship in the main event. Also appears in the AAWA's 25 Aug Battle Royale. Also appears on 27 Aug 1997, beating the CWO's own Television Champion, The Focus, in a cross-promotional singles match (The Focus is not this wing's own roster and is not structured into matches[], per the canonical-copy convention); and on 3 Sep, losing to Dragon Lee after Lee blinds him with a handful of mist.
caption: Challenged Rip Daddy Scorpio for the AAWA World Heavyweight Championship on the premiere Saturday Night Fight and came up short.

name: Green Goblin
notes: Billed from Parts Unknown, accompanied by manager Harry Osborne. Interferes in the Miguel Sanchez/Jeff Easthope match on 13 Aug 1997 (blinding Easthope with powder, causing a no contest), then beats Easthope outright in a No-DQ/submission match on 19 Aug with help from two unnamed Goblin-costumed impostors (retroactively referenced as 'Super and HobGoblin' in the 3 Sep recap montage, never individually named or minted).
caption: A recurring on-screen antagonist to Jeff Easthope, costing him a no contest on 13 Aug 1997 before beating him outright on 19 Aug with the help of two costumed impostors.

notes: Green Goblin's manager; actively interferes rather than merely accompanying -- distracts the referee on 13 Aug 1997 and physically hands/tosses Goblin a chair mid-match on 19 Aug.
